abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) is a highly specialized vascular endothelial network tightly regulating peripheral influences on the brain. BBB endothelial cells (ECs) are mitochondrially rich compared to peripheral ECs, and mitochondrial function has been linked with the induction of BBB properties. In the 22q11.2 deletion syndrome (22qDS), a condition with heightened risk for schizophrenia (SZ), we demonstrated rescue of BBB properties by restoring mitochondrial function. Thus, we sought to understand if energetic and structural capacities of the BBB may influence the SZ penetrance seen in 22qDS. We differentiated induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) from control, 22qDS individuals without SZ (22qDS(-)SZ), and 22qDS individuals with SZ (22qDS + SZ) into BBB-like cells (iBBB). We found that the iBBBs derived from 22qDS + SZ display considerable reductions in the rate of oxygen consumption as compared to 22qDS without (22qDS(-)SZ). Furthermore, 22qDS(-)SZ iBBB retain control-level barrier characteristics, including resistance to ionic flux, and enhanced tight junction and cytoskeletal properties. These phenotypes were further reinforced by RNA sequencing, which implicated several metabolic-, cytoskeletal-, and cell-cell adhesion-related differentially expressed genes, and ontological and gene-set enrichment phenotypes. Together, our functional and transcriptomic data indicate a dual compensation in metabolic and structural programs specific to the 22qDS subgroup lacking a SZ diagnosis. Thus, the penetrance of SZ in the BBB strongly associates with the capacity to maintain structural and metabolic phenotypes, representing a defining feature of 22qDS-related SZ pathophysiology. These findings bridge a gap in knowledge of molecular features which characterize differential phenotypes in the psychosis subtypes of 22qDS and address divergent BBB cell biology between individuals with and without SZ.
